title: 'Once again, an abduction': Aides claim Neha Bora taken to unknown location by cops
content: AISA chief Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police while heading to a protest, and was taken to an unknown location. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke was also detained at his residence shortly before the protest. Police stated the situation remained peaceful despite the detentions and heightened security in the capital. Hundreds of protesters gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House, waving national flags.

title: 'I am alone, broke no law': Dipke argues with Delhi cops as they detain him - watch
content: Dipke, earlier today, had defended the party's protests, asserting that peaceful demonstrations were a democratic right. He accused the government of restricting citizens' freedoms and disrupting business activities through shutdowns, Internet suspensions and movement restrictions. "I'm alone, what law did I break," Dipke asked before he was detained. The court had directed the CJP to refrain from causing any public disturbance for a period of one year.

title: MHA seeks reports from Punjab govt on killings, suicide linked to anti-drug efforts
content: The Ministry of Home Affairs has called for detailed reports from Punjab's authorities concerning two violent occurrences linked to the fight against drugs. The first incident, the murder of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh in Mansa, ignited widespread protests. Meanwhile, an assault on Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur resulted in his death.

title: Anduril CEO defends government contracts: ‘I’m a lifelong Democrat’
content: Anduril Industries, co-founded by Palmer Luckey, has made impressive strides in securing defense contracts from the US government, with CEO Brian Schimpf highlighting the company's persistent growth across different political climates. A recent announcement detailed a substantial contract worth up to $2.9 billion with the US Navy, though questions have been raised about whether Luckey's political ties are influencing these strategic awards.

title: Michigan woman’s survivorship deed upheld over daughter’s challenge
content: A Michigan appeals court has confirmed the validity of a survivorship deed that granted ownership of a house to Jessica Rae Harless. The ruling asserts that Shirley Ann Page's 2012 deed established a joint tenancy with rights of survivorship. Despite Anita Lanctot's challenge regarding the absence of the term 'joint' in the deed, the court affirmed that Page's intent was unmistakably conveyed, ensuring Harless retains sole ownership of the property.

title: 'Ensure safety of Indians': MEA's strong message to US after Hindu temple 'attack' plot
content: Authorities in Aurora thwarted a disturbing mass-shooting scheme aimed at a local Hindu temple. In light of this, the Indian ministry of external affairs voiced alarm over the rise in hate crimes in the United States. A 19-year-old suspect now faces charges for threatening the temple while armed. Meanwhile, Indian-American organizations are mobilizing to spotlight anti-Indian sentiment and exploring collective response strategies.

title: Georgia renter left paralysed by falling tree gets claims revived by appeals court
content: William Frank Jennings, a Lindale, Georgia resident, became paralyzed after a tree fell on his house, despite having warned his landlord about its dangerous state. The Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that his claims against Romulus Investments were improperly dismissed, noting significant conflicting evidence regarding hazard notifications. This ruling enables Jennings to pursue his case further to potentially establish liability and seek damages for his injuries.

title: 'You take up this role to set a culture': Mandhana on the legacy she wants to leave
content: India will face Zimbabwe women's team for the first time in international cricket. The series will also give Mandhana a chance to begin preparing the team for the ICC Women's Champions Trophy 2027, which will be held in India.

title: How much gold and silver can you legally keep at home?
content: In a recent case before the ITAT Mumbai, the Income Tax Department carried out searches at a woman's residence and bank lockers, and seized diamonds, gold and silver articles, along with jewellery, which it treated as unexplained assets. The seized items included gold jewellery of 427.71 grams, 258 grams of pure gold, diamond-studded jewellery containing 161.33 grams of gold, and articles made of a silver mixture weighing 11.200 kg.

title: Court tells US to process Green Card applications for up to 55k people
content: A federal judge has ordered the reopening of the diversity visa lottery for 2027, allowing 55,000 applicants. The ruling came after a lawsuit filed against Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding the lottery's registration. Judge Jinsook Ohta mandated a 30-day registration period for submissions, which must meet eligibility requirements. Additionally, new policy changes require some applicants to return to their home countries for Green Card processing.

title: Texas woman turned homemade soda into Poppi; PepsiCo later bought it for $1.95bn
content: Allison Ellsworth began making homemade soda in her Texas kitchen to address her digestive concerns before selling it at farmers’ markets. After appearing on Shark Tank and building Poppi through social media, her business grew to over $500 million in annual revenue. In 2025, PepsiCo acquired the prebiotic soda brand for $1.95 billion.

title: Rahul alleges Delhi Police refused to file FIR over assault on student protesters
content: Rahul Gandhi alleged that Delhi Police failed to register an FIR regarding the assault on student protesters. He mentioned two young women were among those harmed, prompting legal action against police officers. Detentions occurred ahead of a proposed Tiranga rally in Connaught Place, highlighting increased security measures in the area. Police cited restrictions and prior agreements while detaining activists to maintain public order.

title: Connor McDavid's family: How his parents, brother and wife shaped his NHL career
content: Connor McDavid, the rising NHL superstar, has been helped shape by a family that has supported his development, discipline and life away from hockey. His parents, Brian and Kelly McDavid, encouraged his early dreams, while older brother Cameron provided a competitive edge. He continues his career as captain of the Edmonton Oilers, and his wife, Lauren Kyle, has become a big part of his life personally.

title: Caitlin Clark's family: How her parents and siblings shaped her WNBA journey
content: Caitlin Clark’s road to WNBA stardom was paved by a family that supported her basketball dreams early on; and her father, Brent Clark, taught her the basics and her mother, Anne Clark, gave her emotional support, and her brothers, Blake and Colin, added a competitive element to her upbringing, helping to shape the determination and athletic drive behind her rise.

title: 75,000-year-old Neanderthal injury may be earliest evidence of lethal spear attack
content: A Neanderthal who lived 75,000 years ago survived a severe facial injury for at least a year before suffering a possibly fatal spear wound. Researchers studying remains found in Iraq’s Shanidar Cave identified a 15mm hole in the shoulder blade, suggesting a wooden spear injury. The findings also point to possible care from other Neanderthals.

title: Addison Lee founder’s London mansion once asking £32m sells for £11.5m
content: John Griffin, the mind behind Addison Lee, experienced a substantial loss after selling his lavish London mansion for £11.5 million, down from the £20.7 million he paid in 2013, incurring a staggering loss of £9.2 million. This sale reflects the broader downturn in London's property landscape, impacted by economic instability and new tax regulations.

title: He paid Rs 15L for Rs 10L flat; builder demanded Rs 20 lakh more, buyer wins case
content: A man, who was working in the US, booked a 1,208-square-foot flat along with a car parking space in Patna. The booking was confirmed in 2005, and the agreement for sale was signed in 2007. The total price agreed upon for the flat and parking space was Rs 10,41,250. Before the agreement was executed, the man had already paid Rs 9 lakh to the builder.

title: Husband strangled, snake placed beside body: UP court awards death penalty to wife, lover
content: Ravita and Amardeep received the death penalty for the murder of Amit Kashyap in Meerut. They staged the crime scene to resemble a snakebite, raising initial suspicions among family members. A post-mortem revealed that he had died from strangulation rather than a snakebite. The judge emphasized the need to support Ravita's children following the ruling. Both accused were present for the verdict via video conferencing in court.

title: Kelce brothers’ $33.5M Stoney Clover Lane deal: What’s changing for New Heights merch?
content: Jason and Travis Kelce have partnered with Stoney Clover Lane to launch a New Heights-inspired collection featuring clear stadium bags, a fanny pack, pouches and custom patches. The accessories celebrate the brothers' podcast and its 92 percenters fanbase while combining practical designs with playful details. Available through the Kelce Clubhouse, the collection coincides with the launch of its "Outta The House" hub and upcoming in-person fan events.

title: 'She’s in power because of me': Rekha Arya’s husband releases video, calls her 'corrupt'
content: Rekha Arya, a cabinet minister in Uttarakhand, has filed a police complaint against her husband Girdhari Lal Sahu. She accused him of physical assault, harassment, and making death threats towards her. In response, Sahu released a video alleging that Arya's claims are based on an AI-generated audio clip. Arya has alleged corruption against Sahu, claiming he is responsible for her political rise.

title: 'Things got excessive after divorce': Yuzvendra Chahal opens up on alcohol addiction
content: Yuzvendra Chahal revealed his struggles with alcohol following his divorce and the importance of rehabilitation. He checked into a rehab centre for 26 days to regain control over his life. Chahal emphasized that he recognized the need to stop drinking to protect his cricket career. While he has faced personal challenges, he remains a leading wicket-taker in the IPL. His experiences have contributed to his emotional maturity and overall well-being.

title: 'Can't replace capability': Starlink disruption exposes Ukraine's reliance on US tech
content: EU leaders are addressing concerns regarding Ukraine's reliance on Elon Musk's Starlink satellite for military communications. Disruptions to the Starlink service have highlighted the urgent need for European alternatives. Officials discussed how to strengthen Europe's satellite communication capabilities during a recent summit with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Investor interest in European satellite companies, such as Eutelsat and SES, has surged after the disruptions.

title: Dak Prescott's $240 million Cowboys contract in 2024 included $231 million guaranteed
content: Dak Prescott signed a four-year, $240 million contract extension with the Dallas Cowboys in September 2024, including $231 million in total guaranteed money and an $80 million signing bonus. The deal made him the NFL’s highest-paid player by average annual value at $60 million per season. Dallas secured its franchise quarterback through 2028, betting on his leadership and passing ability to end the team’s long Super Bowl drought.

title: NBA star Deandre Ayton pledges $100,000 to rebuild Jamaica after 2025 hurricane
content: Deandre Ayton demonstrates his dedication to community service through his active participation in the PMBL Youth Basketball Camp in Jamaica. His Ayton Family Foundation engages in vital hurricane recovery efforts and provides access to food resources. This camp annually welcomes over 1,500 children, offering free meals, supplies, and enriching experiences.

title: Tennessee man turns backyard pool into 500,000-gallon water playground
content: In Covington, Tennessee, Micky Thornton transformed a childhood aspiration into reality by building a vast backyard pool. Initially a family retreat, this impressive space evolved into a gathering hub, hosting everything from birthday celebrations to weddings. Notably, it has become a venue for over 400 baptisms, deepening its community ties. Thornton's journey showcases that the pursuit of extraordinary dreams demands patience and dedication to refining one’s vision.

title: UK shopper paid £1 for first-edition James Bond book; it later sold for £10,000
content: A woman bought a book at a car boot sale in Yorkshire for just £1 ten years ago. She later discovered it was a rare first edition of Casino Royale by Ian Fleming. The book retained its original dust jacket and was valued significantly. It was auctioned for £10,000, highlighting the importance of rarity and condition in collectibles. The successful bidder was a UK collector specializing in Ian Fleming editions.

title: Taylor Swift gave 6,000 books to struggling library; 15 years later, it thrives
content: In 2011, Taylor Swift generously donated 6,000 books to bolster local libraries in Berks County amid looming budget cuts. This pivotal support allowed the Reading Public Library to enrich its programs and attract thousands of community members. By 2025, the library circulated over 182,000 items and continued to foster engagement through various initiatives, proving Swift’s contribution remains vital for the region's library services to this day.

title: Black ink on Tagore: The fight over Bangladesh's identity
content: The recent defacement of Rabindranath Tagore's portrait in Dhaka has stirred a fresh wave of conversations about his legacy. Against the backdrop of increased political unease post the July 2024 uprising and claims against Jamaat-e-Islami, public outcry highlights the threat to cultural icons. This event has mobilized protests and reinvigorated discussions, reflecting on the vital intersection of politics, culture, and the essence of national identity in contemporary Bangladesh.

title: Fish gasp for oxygen in ‘cleanest’ Yamuna stretch, greens raise a stink
content: Shocking images recently released show countless dead fish littering the banks of the Yamuna River near Wazirabad, prompting urgent discussions about pollution. Fishermen had previously noted a strong, unpleasant odor from the river, raising alarms. An environmental organization is now demanding immediate investigations and water sampling upstream to uncover the cause behind this die-off.

title: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards in 2027; first time in over 70 years
content: Pakistan will assume the chairmanship of the IMF and World Bank Group boards in 2027, marking a significant return. This follows a long absence from the position that last occurred in 1953. The role will allow Pakistan to engage in global economic discussions and foster collaboration among member nations. Pakistan is currently utilizing financial assistance from the IMF through various programs aimed at economic stabilization.

title: Staying connected under fire: How GSAT-7C will boost IAF's fighting edge
content: The Indian Air Force signed a deal for the GSAT-7C satellite to boost its communications capabilities. This satellite aims to enhance secure communications for network-centric warfare beyond traditional networks. It is designed to facilitate real-time connectivity, allowing various military platforms to communicate effectively. Developing this satellite domestically reduces reliance on foreign providers, enhancing India's military autonomy. However, details regarding its specifications and launch date have not been disclosed.

title: Miley Cyrus foundation gives $1m toward 97 permanent homes for women in LA
content: Miley Cyrus' foundation has pledged $1 million towards Rosa's Place, a housing project in Los Angeles that will provide 97 permanent apartments for women and survivors of violence experiencing homelessness. The donation was announced at the Downtown Women's Center's annual gala, which raised $3.2 million. The development in Skid Row is expected to open in 2027.

title: Japan issued a 9.9 magnitude earthquake alert, but ground didn't shake: What happened
content: An "alert" indicating a massive magnitude-9.9 earthquake sent shockwaves of fear across Japan on Friday afternoon. Just eight minutes after its issuance, the Japan Meteorological Agency retracted the warning, which had been triggered by a lesser magnitude-6.9 quake off the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia. Although the alert caused temporary disruptions in transportation, officials are now investigating the warning system to ensure public safety and prevent future confusion.

title: New York pays $28.25m to protect nearly 750 acres once reserved for nuclear plant
content: New York has purchased nearly 750 acres surrounding the former Shoreham Nuclear Power Plant on Long Island for $28.25 million. The acquisition, the largest in the history of the state's Department of Environmental Conservation on Long Island, will permanently protect coastal forests, wetlands and wildlife habitats. The state also plans to develop public trails, parking facilities and beach access in the coming years.

title: ‘I was terrified’: Chahal on being hung from balcony by ‘heavily drunk’ cricketer
content: Yuzvendra Chahal shared a chilling memory from his IPL journey that involved an Australian cricketer back in 2013. During a Royal Challengers Bengaluru party, he found himself dangerously suspended over a hotel balcony by an inebriated player. Terrified and with onlookers present, he was soon rescued. This episode has since propelled Chahal to concentrate on his cricket aspirations while embodying the hope of an international comeback.

title: Bought Hyundai Eon in 2016 but got no RC or invoice; commission orders Rs 22,500 payout

The commission dismissed Hyundai's argument of being exempt from the dealer's responsibilities and mandated the company to compensate Singh for emotional distress and legal expenses. This decision underscores the obligation manufacturers have to ensure their dealers uphold service standards.
